title: Stream adaptor UX + Tool Delegation — Sprint Journal
body:
Context and intent:
This sprint journal captures a compact, engineering-first RFC and working notes for a streaming adaptor that makes progressive structured output and tool delegation ergonomics easy to adopt for application developers. The goal is to converge on a minimal, composable client surface that supports: resumable partial streams, clear backpressure signals, explicit tool-handshake frames, and developer-friendly fallbacks for low-bandwidth or offline clients.

Why now:
- We keep hearing adoption friction from customers who need typed tool outputs but don’t want to adopt a heavy SDK.
- Mobile and embedded clients report dropped connections; resumability and compact snapshots are high ROI.
- We can reduce server-side wasted compute by enabling speculative prefetch and early offload to local proxies.

High-level design principles (working):
1) Bounded, immutable frames: streams are a sequence of small, self-describing frames (text delta, json patch, tool-handshake, checkpoint). Each frame must be parseable independently to allow partial rendering and replay.
2) Explicit tool handshake: tool invocation is a two-phase frame exchange — INVOKE -> ACCEPT/REJECT -> RESULT( streaming ). The client can opt into optimistic acceptance to reduce latency.
3) Single-surface SDK: one small client package (JS/TS + minimal Python) exposing the same verbs: openStream(), resumeStream(token), callTool(toolSpec, opts).
4) Cost and latency signals: include token-cost-estimate and slog hints in frames to help clients decide to abort, downgrade fidelity, or route to local proxy.
5) Observability-first: each frame carries a compact tracing header (sampled trace id) and a semantic event code for post-hoc QA and regressions.

Scope for this sprint:
- Prototype an SDK surface for web + node that demonstrates resumable streams, tool handshake, and structured JSON fragments.
- Validate a small server-side frame schema and produce test vectors.
- Run playbook with two customers: mobile chat app and enterprise workflow automations to capture failure modes.

User stories (prioritized):
- As a mobile app engineer, I want to show partial results as soon as they arrive and recover them after a reconnect so the user sees progress instead of an error.
- As a backend engineer, I want to delegate a search-tool call and receive structured results that can be validated and re-streamed without re-invoking the model.
- As a platform operator, I want each tool-call frame to include cost estimates and trace keys so I can attribute spikes to specific tool delegations.

Proposed frame grammar (human-readable sketch):
- FRAME {type, id, prev_id?, payload, meta}
  - types: TEXT_DELTA | JSON_PATCH | TOOL_INVOKE | TOOL_ACK | TOOL_RESULT_CHUNK | CHECKPOINT | RESUME_TOKEN | ERROR
  - meta: {trace_id, cost_estimate, fidelity_hint}

Tool handshake flow (example):
1) client sends TOOL_INVOKE(tool: {name: 'search', params}) as part of stream
2) server responds with TOOL_ACK(id, accepted: true|false, exec_profile_hint)
3) server emits TOOL_RESULT_CHUNK frames (structured) streamed as they arrive
4) final TOOL_RESULT_CHUNK with meta.status = 'complete' and optional CHECKPOINT emitted

SDK ergonomics proposal (JS pseudocode):
- openStream({prompt, onFrame, onProgress}) -> returns {streamId, cancel, getCheckpoint}
- resumeStream(resumeToken, {onFrame}) -> returns stream handle
- callTool(toolSpec, {inline: true|false, onPartial}) -> returns promise for final result or stream handle if inline streaming enabled

Example usage (web):
const s = await openStream({ prompt });
s.onFrame(frame => { if (frame.type === 'TEXT_DELTA') renderDelta(frame.payload); });
// optimistic tool call inside stream
callTool({ name: 'kb-lookup', q: 'pricing' }, { inline: true }).onPartial(p => showSuggestion(p));

Failure and fallback modes to account for:
- Client disconnects before TOOL_ACK: server should emit an idempotent resume token in the next checkpoint so the client can re-issue the invoke without double-exec.
- Tool execution heavy tail: server offers a 'degrade-to-summary' hint to client with a compact summary frame to preserve UX.
- Partial JSON patch conflict: include a patch-base checksum in frame meta; if mismatch on resume, surface a deterministic fallback (apply from last checkpoint).

Observability and QA signals:
- Each frame includes cost_estimate (low/medium/high), trace_id, and event_code (e.g., TE_TOOL_START, TE_TOOL_CHUNK, TE_CHECKPOINT).
- Add a post-run regression harness that replays saved frame sequences (golden transcripts) against new server builds; flag structured-output diffs.

Performance and cost considerations:
- Encourage clients to prefer JSON_PATCH frames for structured content to reduce token churn versus verbose textual re-generation.
- Server-side batching: tool-result-chunks can be batched across concurrent streams when routing to the same backend tool to reduce outward calls.
- Prefetch heuristics: server may speculatively call a cached local tool if the client has indicated high-probability tool hints in the first frame.

Security and safety notes:
- Tool invocation schema must be validated against allowlists per-customer in Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Audit log: every TOOL_INVOKE and TOOL_ACK frame logged with minimal PII; CHECKPOINTs should be redactable.

Migration and compatibility plan:
- Support a minimal compatibility layer so existing non-streaming endpoints can return a single CHECKPOINT frame representing full response.
- Offer a 'compat-mode' flag in openStream that sends legacy-friendly TEXT_DELTA only.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Internal prototype: small node demo + web client (2 weeks) — collect sample transcripts.
2) Beta with two customers under NDA (mobile app + enterprise automation) (6 weeks) — focus on resume semantics and tool-handshake reliability.
3) Public SDK alpha with telemetry and golden-run validation (4 weeks).

Risks and open questions (tracked):
- How large should a checkpoint token be? tradeoff: frequency vs. token size for resume reliability.
- Backpressure semantics with long-running tools: how do we surface cancellation in a cross-client-friendly manner?
- SDK surface: promise-based streaming vs. async iterator — which is easier for integration across languages? (collect telemetries from early adopters)

Next steps (this sprint):
- Liam: implement server frame serializer & sample test vectors (due 2025-02-18).
- Marisol: prototype the JS client openStream/resumeStream API and a small page showing resume after simulated disconnect (due 2025-02-20).
- Ethan: draft observability event schema and integrate with tracing in the trace-agent (due 2025-02-21).
- Asha: prepare customer playbook and consent language for beta tests (due 2025-02-22).

Notes to reviewers:
- Look for API ergonomics that reduce integration surface area; avoid forcing users to manage low-level frames unless they want to.
- Pay special attention to resume semantics — correctness trumps micro-optimizations in early rollouts.
- Please add references to any existing SDK ideas that would simplify the proposal (e.g., async iterators in Node, or small web worker patterns for mobile).

Appendix: quick test vector examples (JSON lines):
{"frame":{"type":"TEXT_DELTA","id":"f1","payload":"Hey, I found","meta":{"trace_id":"t1","cost_estimate":"low"}}}
{"frame":{"type":"TOOL_INVOKE","id":"t-inv-1","payload":{"tool":"search","q":"redwood pricing"},"meta":{"trace_id":"t1"}}}
{"frame":{"type":"TOOL_ACK","id":"t-ack-1","payload":{"accepted":true},"meta":{"trace_id":"t1"}}}
{"frame":{"type":"TOOL_RESULT_CHUNK","id":"t-res-1","payload":{"items":[{"title":"pricing","id":12}]},"meta":{"trace_id":"t1","cost_estimate":"medium"}}}
{"frame":{"type":"CHECKPOINT","id":"cp1","payload":{"resume_token":"r-xxxxx","cursor":"cp1"},"meta":{"trace_id":"t1"}}}

(End of sprint journal)
